Evaluate a track expression under single-base substitutions

Source: R/compute-variants.R
gextract.variants.Rd

For each iterator bin, evaluates expr once on the reference genome and once for every single-base substitution the bin's sequence virtual tracks read: all three alternative bases at each base in reach (the default), or the variants listed in variants.

Usage

gextract.variants(
  expr = NULL,
  intervals = NULL,
  variants = NULL,
  iterator = NULL,
  score.thresh = NULL,
  colnames = NULL
)

Arguments

expr

a track expression with at least one sequence virtual track.

intervals

genomic scope, as in gextract.

variants

NULL for every substitution in reach, or a data frame with columns chrom, start (0-based), ref and alt, such as the output of gintervals.import_vcf. A variant whose ref does not match the genome gets a warning and NA in <name>.alt; <name>.ref keeps the reference value.

iterator

track expression iterator, as in gextract.

score.thresh

if not NULL, keep only the rows where the reference value and the substituted value fall on different sides of it.

colnames

name used for the value columns, <name>.ref and <name>.alt; the expression itself by default.

Value

A data frame with one row per (bin, substitution): the bin's chrom, start and end; the substitution's pos (0-based), ref and alt; <name>.ref and <name>.alt; and intervalID as in gextract. NULL when there is no row.

Details

A bin [s, e) of a sequence virtual track reads [s + sshift, e + eshift + W - 1), where the shifts come from gvtrack.iterator and W - 1 is added when the track extends (extend = TRUE, motif or model width W). pwm.edit_distance with max_indels reads further: it ends max_indels bases later, at e + eshift + W - 1 + max_indels. A substitution is paired with every bin whose reach, the union over the expression's sequence virtual tracks, contains it. Tracks and non-sequence virtual tracks in expr are read as usual, so they contribute the same value to both columns. The substituted base takes the case of the reference base, so masked.* tracks see the same mask. Only single-base substitutions are supported.

The exact pass runs in one process. For genome-scale runs, split intervals by chromosome and run the pieces in parallel.

Run genome-wide, every bin returns about three rows per base in reach. To find the bins one substitution can move across a threshold, screen first with a bound (for example from potts.max virtual tracks with max_edits = 1) and pass the result as intervals, with score.thresh.

See also

gextract, gvtrack.create, gintervals.import_vcf

Examples


gdb.init_examples()
pssm <- matrix(c(
    0.7, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1,
    0.1, 0.7, 0.1, 0.1,
    0.1, 0.1, 0.7, 0.1
), ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE, dimnames = list(NULL, c("A", "C", "G", "T")))
gvtrack.create("motif", NULL, "pwm.max", params = list(pssm = pssm, bidirect = FALSE))
gextract.variants("motif", gintervals(1, 100, 102), iterator = 1)
